title: Maintenance and commissioning engineering software
description: Maintenance and commissioning in E1: Deep view of everything linked to an object, redlining on live diagrams and on the iPad, tasks, technical and engineering queries, a chat on every object, and commissioning packages in branches.
h1: Maintenance and commissioning, on the live plant model.
lead: In E1, the plant you maintain and commission is the same model the engineers designed. Open any object and see everything linked to it, mark up the live diagrams in the office or on site, raise a technical or engineering query where the question is, talk about an object on the object itself, and collect finished work into a commissioning package.

glance.label: From an object to everything linked to it, in Deep view
Task types, including Technical query and Engineering query
Places to work: the desktop, the iPad and the phone

sections.h2: Deep view: everything linked to an object, at a glance
sections.intro: Deep view shows an object and every object associated with it, as a data model of cards and links, like an object diagram rather than a drawing. You open it layer by layer with +1, or all at once with Expand all, until nothing more is linked.
paragraphs: From a valve you follow the pipes on its ports to the pump beyond, the transmitter that measures the pump, its terminals, the cable core landed on them, the cable and the junction box at its other end. Before you isolate, replace or test something, you see what it touches.

Click a card to see its values and links, with Open, Show in tree and Deep view of this. Highlight route draws the way from one card to another in bold while everything else fades; Find in view outlines the cards whose tag, name, class or value holds your text; a chip for each kind of link shows or hides those links.
bullets: Opened from the object window's Deep view tab, or from a symbol on a 2D space: right-click → Open ▸ Deep view.
The bar under the view counts the objects, links and levels shown, and the cards that have more to show.

sections.intro: In E1, you mark up a 2D space with clouds, arrows, text, pins and stamps on a Markups layer that never changes the drawing, and each markup is discussed in its own card.
paragraphs: Every markup has a status and a response: accept, reject, answer, incorporate or close. Each change is written in its discussion and tells its author, so nothing raised on site is lost on the way back to the office.

The Markups list filters a 2D space's markups and runs a review round with its reviewers; when it is closed, the comment resolution sheet is exported. A marked-up print carries each markup as a real PDF comment, and a reviewer's annotated PDF reads back into E1 as markups in the round.

sections.h2: On site with the iPad and the phone
sections.intro: E1 Reviewer for iPad and E1 Mobile for iPhone and Android launch with E1 on 19 May 2027, on the same model.
paragraphs: On the iPad, every drawing goes to site. Redline it with a pen, a cloud, an arrow, text or a stamp; each mark says what it means and carries a note, goes into a review round and is answered by the engineers in E1. Tap a symbol, a pipe, a signal or a cable to see its object: its properties, every attribute, its history and its chat.
On the phone, messages, tasks and Alex are in your pocket, typed or spoken. Everything lands in the same E1 model at once.

sections.h2: Tasks, technical queries and engineering queries
sections.intro: In E1, a question about the plant is a task for a person or a group, not an e-mail.
paragraphs: New task… offers E1's seven task types, including Technical query and Engineering query, and your organization's own, each a task or a query. A task has a type, a due date, a description and a screenshot, once or repeating; the people it is for see it in their Inbox and mark it done.
A task can carry a checklist of items to tick, in the Inbox in E1 and the same in E1 Reviewer on the iPad.

sections.intro: In E1, every object has a Chat tab: the conversation about a pump, a valve or a cable stays with that pump, valve or cable.
paragraphs: @mention a colleague to bring them in, #link another object, reply, like, edit, delete and resolve. Whoever opens the object later reads why it is the way it is.

sections.h2: Modifications and commissioning packages in branches
sections.intro: In E1, a plant modification is made in a branch while the shared design stays untouched, and finished work is collected into a commissioning package.
paragraphs: Collect finished work into a commissioning package by drawing around it or by right-click, give it its dates, lead and description, then mark it ready and push it to main on its own. Every change is recorded and compared before it lands.

faq.q: What is Deep view in E1?
faq.a: Deep view shows an object and every object associated with it as cards and links. You open it layer by layer or all at once, highlight the route between two objects and find any object in the view.

faq.q: Can I raise a technical query in E1?
faq.a: Yes. New task… offers Technical query and Engineering query among E1's seven task types, and your organization can add its own.

faq.q: Can I redline drawings on site?
faq.a: Yes. In E1 you mark up any 2D space on a Markups layer, and E1 Reviewer for iPad, launching on 19 May 2027, redlines on site with the marks answered by the engineers in E1.
